questions.problem: For what value of $k$ are the lines $2x-4y=8$ and $kx+2y=12$ parallel?
questions.worked_solution:
For two lines to be parallel, they must have the same slope.

- To find the slope of the line $2x-4y=8,$ we convert to slope-intercept form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}2x-4y & =8 \\ -4y & =-2x+8 \\ 4y & =2x-8 \\ y & =\frac{1}{2}x-2\end{aligned}
$$

In slope-intercept form, the slope is the $x$-coefficient. So, the slope is $\frac{1}{2}.$

- To find the slope of the line $kx+2y=12,$ we convert to slope-intercept form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}kx+2y & =12 \\ 2y & =-kx+12 \\ y & =-\frac{k}{2}x+6\end{aligned}
$$

In slope-intercept form, the slope is the $x$-coefficient. So, the slope is $-\frac{k}{2}.$

Since the slopes of the two lines must be equal, we must have $-\frac{k}{2}=\frac{1}{2}.$ We solve for $k:$

$$
\begin{aligned}-\frac{k}{2} & =\frac{1}{2} \\ \frac{k}{2} & =-\frac{1}{2} \\ k & =-1\end{aligned}
$$

I. $y=4x-8$

II. $y=12x+1$

III. $y=3x-12$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
For two lines to be parallel, they must have the same slope.

To find the slope of the line $12x-y=3,$ we convert to slope-intercept form:

$$
\begin{aligned}12x-y & =3 \\ -y & =-12x+3 \\ y & =12x-3.\end{aligned}
$$

In slope-intercept form, the slope is the $x$-coefficient. So, the slope is $12.$

canonical_examples.problem: The lines $y=2x$ and $kx-2y=-1$ are parallel. What is the value of $k?$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
For two lines to be parallel, they must have the same slope.

- The line $y=2x$ is in slope-intercept form, and its slope is $2.$

- To find the slope of the line $kx-2y=-1,$ we convert to slope-intercept form:

$$
\begin{aligned}kx-2y & =-1 \\ -2y & =-kx-1 \\ 2y & =kx+1 \\ y & =\frac{k}{2}x+\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

In slope-intercept form, the slope is the $x$-coefficient. So, the slope is $\dfrac{k}{2}.$

Since the slopes of the two lines must be equal, we must have $\dfrac{k}{2}=2.$ Consequently, $k=4.$

tutorials.name: Introduction
tutorials.problem:
Two distinct lines that never intersect are said to be **parallel.** For two lines to be parallel, they must have the same slope. 

For example, the lines $y=2x+4$ and $y=2x-5$ have the same slope of $m=2,$ so they are parallel. Indeed, looking at the graph, we see that the two lines never cross.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14189267/assets/c7d36372d9646d0ce10eff5d35a4f9b8e56a7b37b333c5d53ac243065ee751af.png)

On the other hand, the lines $y=\dfrac{1}{2}x+4$ and $y=2x-5$ have different slopes, so they are *not* parallel. Indeed, looking at the graph, we see that the two lines *do* cross.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14189267/assets/92c1ee39ccbbbf20dc3f4a7f76a1114d975fb0826eeac13d273b4b4fd9a83105.png)
